thread.title_full: Military veteran balances studies and family life at Montana State University

author: yellowstone times
title: Military veteran balances studies and family life at Montana State University
text:
Montana State University junior James Mayfield IV is pursuing a history teaching degree while balancing family responsibilities and military service. A U.S. Marine veteran and current Navy Reserves corpsman, Mayfield aims to graduate in 2027 and will soon welcome his second child.
Originally from Douglasville, Georgia, Mayfield moved to Montana without having visited the state before. His decision to leave Georgia came after caring for his father, who suffered a stroke during Mayfield’s last year in the Marine Corps. “My father had a stroke my last year when I was in the Marine Corps,” he said. “It’s part of the reason I got out. So, I went home to Georgia to take care of him.”
Mayfield has become known at MSU for his willingness to support others. Todd Bucher, director of Veteran Services at MSU’s Travis W. Atkins Veteran Support Center, described him as someone who prioritizes others: “James is the kind of person who naturally puts others before himself,” Bucher said. “Whether it’s lending a hand to a fellow student, supporting his family or stepping up in his community, James consistently goes the extra mile. He’s the first to arrive, the last to leave and the one quietly making sure everyone else has what they need before thinking of himself.”
Mayfield noted that even before arriving on campus in fall 2023, he was already communicating with Bucher regarding GI Bill matters. “Todd is one of the first people I was in communication with since he handles [matters pertaining to] the GI Bill,” Mayfield said. “He’s just an outstanding human being; he’s been great for myself and my family. My little daughter loves him.”
His wife Kalli is also involved with MSU as a part-time elementary education major and plans to pursue social work after graduation.
Mayfield also credits Joshua Meyer, director of MSU’s McNair Scholars Program—which supports nontraditional students—for providing additional support during his academic journey: “[Meyer], too, is an outstanding human being,” Mayfield said. “It’s nice to have another person to talk to about life matters [beyond school].” The program helps increase post-baccalaureate degree attainment among students who have not traditionally participated in higher education.
Tim LeCain, chair of MSU’s Department of History and Philosophy, highlighted Mayfield’s experience: “James is a remarkable guy who’s already led a fascinating life,” LeCain said. “His military service has put him on the front lines of a lot of recent events that historians will be discussing for years to come. He was in for advising recently, and we ended up talking for almost an hour about all sorts of things. The history faculty is honored to have him in our program.”
After completing his undergraduate studies at Montana State University, Mayfield plans on attending graduate school.
